meta.title: Order Lookup: Validate and Parameterize
meta.subtitle: Review untrusted request input, correct unsafe query construction and verify the pattern did not return elsewhere.

brief.role: You are reviewing a fictional TypeScript order-lookup change before merge.
brief.context: The endpoint accepts an order identifier from a request. Inspect how the value is handled, request the right correction, then use the simulated checks to find a similar regression in a shared helper.
brief.safetyNote: Training data only. The files contain fictional code and no real guest, employee or production data.

mission.objective: Ensure untrusted request values are validated and bound as data, not interpreted as SQL.

achievements.title: Clean inspection
achievements.description: Completed the mission without using a hint.

achievements.title: Query pattern spotter
achievements.description: Recognized the same unsafe query pattern in a different artifact.

stages.title: Mark every line that leaves request input unsafe
stages.instruction: Select the lines that accept unvalidated input or turn it into executable SQL.
hints: Client and route parameters are untrusted even when the user is signed in.
Look for the value entering the route and for a query built by joining that value into SQL.

feedback.correct: You found both parts of the problem: the request value is not validated for the expected type and it is concatenated into a SQL string.
feedback.incorrect: Review both how the request value enters the route and how the database receives it.

feedbackByMissing.order-route:2: A request parameter is not proof of a valid positive order identifier. Validate type, format and range on the server.
feedbackByMissing.order-route:4: Concatenating the value into the query lets untrusted input be interpreted by the SQL interpreter.

concept.label: Validate input and bind it as query data

stages.title: Choose the correction to request
stages.instruction: Select the change that protects the route without relying on the client or a fragile character filter.

choices.label: Remove quotes and semicolons, then keep the string-built query
choices.detail: Use a deny-list to remove known dangerous characters.
choices.feedback: Character stripping is a fragile deny-list. Encodings and edge cases can bypass it, and the query still treats input as code.

choices.label: Validate a positive integer on the server and use a parameterized query
choices.detail: Bind the order identifier as data rather than concatenating it into SQL.

choices.label: Keep the query because the endpoint requires sign-in
choices.feedback: Authentication does not make request data trustworthy. An authenticated caller can still send malicious input.

hints: The fix needs both a server-side allow-list check and a query API that binds values as data.
Choose the option that never joins the request value into the SQL text.

feedback.correct: The corrected route validates the expected identifier and passes it to the database as data, not code.
feedback.incorrect: That option still relies on client trust, deny-listing or string-built SQL.

onCorrect.workspaceStatus: Route corrected · shared-helper finding requires review

stages.title: Run the simulated route checks
stages.instruction: Use the checks as evidence, then inspect the remaining finding rather than assuming the first correction cleared the whole change.

results.message: The route rejects identifiers that are not positive integers.
The route still accepts an unvalidated request value.
The route binds the identifier as a query parameter.
The route still constructs SQL by joining input into query text.
A shared helper still builds a query with string concatenation.

feedback.failed: The primary route is safer, but verification found the same pattern in a different artifact. Review the helper before clearing the merge.

stages.title: Find the query regression in the shared helper
stages.instruction: Apply the same rule in this new context: select the line that treats an input value as part of SQL.
hints: A helper does not make string-built SQL safe.
Find the line where the input value is joined into the query text.

feedback.correct: You recognized the same risk across a route and a shared helper. Parameterization is required wherever input reaches the database.
feedback.incorrect: The unsafe pattern is the line that combines an input value with SQL text.

feedbackByMissing.query-helper:2: The helper concatenates its id argument into SQL. Bind the value through the database API instead.

concept.label: Validate input and bind it as query data

completion.title: The lookup handles input as data
completion.message: You validated untrusted input, used a parameterized query and recognized the same risk when it reappeared in a shared helper.
takeaways: Client controls and authentication do not replace server-side validation.
Use allow-lists for expected type, format and range before a value reaches a sensitive operation.
Bind query values as data; never concatenate untrusted input into SQL.
